_source: Watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18 (Algorithmswithpeter, 5K subs, 401K views, 2 months old). Frames every 0.5 s for 2 s, then every 15-20 s; no sound probe. Shots approximate (pages change every ~5-10 s). Our own descriptions.

hook.firstFrame: an off-white paper page, nearly empty; by 0.5 s a cut-out cartoon man in a suit appears bottom-left beside a two-column comparison card

shots.picture: paper page with serif headings: two language names in boxes, cartoon cut-out host bottom-left
page heading 'Memory management' with a small table and a notes card
a grid of black and beige squares like a memory map, then a chart and code panels
pages of curves, code blocks and seesaw-style comparisons, host fixed bottom-left
more editorial pages: small tables of numbers, labelled boxes, host fixed
page turns dark: verdict cards for each language, host grows bigger at the end

lines.gist: which backend language wins this year
speed, safety and how hard each is to learn
where each one is actually used
pick one for shipping fast, the other for raw performance

ending.lastFrame: dark verdict page with the cartoon host large in the middle

whyItWorks: a versus question developers argue about, settled in one Short
a calm editorial paper look (serif, beige, black) that reads like a premium magazine
a familiar cartoon host as the voice (a borrowed character: never something we copy)
